source: Book IV printed p.73 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.79 (Experiment 2 procedure, no new wiring), wiring printed p.72 = PDF p.78 (Experiment 1, 44 wires), table printed p.68 = PDF p.74, image-read; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the 44-wire Experiment 1 counter (programs.json IV-EXP2 wiresEffective) and the p.73 rule, not printed. ER-22 is a conditional substitution (use the alternate counter if necessary), not a wire edit, so the book circuit runs. Topology: three single-input flip-flops, A = relays 1/2, B = relays 3/4, C = relays 5/6; each odd relay latches through its set-1 N.O. (1G, 3G, 5G at plus) onto the F node shared with its even relay and with output lamp 4, 5 or 6; pushbutton 6 (6Y plus, 6X) feeds C through 5J/6H/5N; C carries to B through 5N-5L-6L-6K to 3J, and B to A through 3N-3L-4L-4K to 1J, each only while the pushbutton is down and the stage is falling from 1 to 0; A has no carry-out. Each push-and-release adds 1 modulo 8, so the count after k pushes from power-on is k mod 8 on relays 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and lights 4, 5, 6. Asserted: relay states, lights 4-6, and only the lamps that carry no current (both indicator lamps and the E-node output lamp of any flip-flop at 0); lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 sit in a coil's series path, often two lamps in parallel, so their class is analog and not derived. Checkpoints at 0 (power-on), 2, 5, 8 and 10 pushes; 0 and 8 are not printed on p.73 (8 applies the printed three-bit rule). Press and release timing copies IV-EXP2; the page prints no timing. Release steps carry the counter collapse tag.

script.cite: Book IV printed p.73 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.79, Experiment 2 para 1 (the counter adds the number of pushes to the number it holds); starting count 0 at power-on is unprinted; derived from topology: plus reaches the counter only at the relay 1, 3, 5 set-1 N.O. contacts (1G, 3G, 5G) and at the pushbutton 6 arm (6Y); each flip-flop's F node (1F/2F/4A, 3F/4F/5A, 5F/6F/6A) is plus only while its odd relay is latched through its own N.O. (nG-nH), and floats otherwise; a flip-flop at 0 has every node floating, so both its relays rest and its indicator lamps and its output lamp on the E node (outLamp1 on 2E, outLamp2 on 4E, outLamp3 on 6E) carry no current; a flip-flop at 1 has both relays operated (odd relay held through its own indicator lamp, even relay fed from the shared F node) and puts outLamp4, 5 or 6 across the rail; lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 share coil current and are not asserted; at power-on every armature starts at rest and no N.O. contact or pushbutton closes, so every relay stays released and all twelve lamps are dark (000)
script.quote: It is possible to perform additions very simply on a Binary Counter. We have already seen that it is possible to add 1 to the number in the counter merely by pushing and releasing pushbutton 6.

script.cite: Book IV printed p.73 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.79, Experiment 2 para 2 (2 pushes displays binary 2); relay and dark-lamp states derived from topology: plus reaches the counter only at the relay 1, 3, 5 set-1 N.O. contacts (1G, 3G, 5G) and at the pushbutton 6 arm (6Y); each flip-flop's F node (1F/2F/4A, 3F/4F/5A, 5F/6F/6A) is plus only while its odd relay is latched through its own N.O. (nG-nH), and floats otherwise; a flip-flop at 0 has every node floating, so both its relays rest and its indicator lamps and its output lamp on the E node (outLamp1 on 2E, outLamp2 on 4E, outLamp3 on 6E) carry no current; a flip-flop at 1 has both relays operated (odd relay held through its own indicator lamp, even relay fed from the shared F node) and puts outLamp4, 5 or 6 across the rail; lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 share coil current and are not asserted; count 2 = 010: flip-flop B (relays 3, 4) at 1, A and C at 0
script.quote: For example, to add 2 and 3: push and release pushbutton 6 twice; the counter will display the binary number 2.

script.cite: Book IV printed p.73 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.79, Experiment 2 para 2 (2 + 3 = 5, the same as 5 pushes) and para 4; bit pattern from printed p.68 = PDF p.74, THE FIRST TEN BINARY NUMBERS AND THEIR DECIMAL EQUIVALENTS row 5 = 101 (Step 7 notes IV-EXP2: light 5 at count 5); derived from topology: plus reaches the counter only at the relay 1, 3, 5 set-1 N.O. contacts (1G, 3G, 5G) and at the pushbutton 6 arm (6Y); each flip-flop's F node (1F/2F/4A, 3F/4F/5A, 5F/6F/6A) is plus only while its odd relay is latched through its own N.O. (nG-nH), and floats otherwise; a flip-flop at 0 has every node floating, so both its relays rest and its indicator lamps and its output lamp on the E node (outLamp1 on 2E, outLamp2 on 4E, outLamp3 on 6E) carry no current; a flip-flop at 1 has both relays operated (odd relay held through its own indicator lamp, even relay fed from the shared F node) and puts outLamp4, 5 or 6 across the rail; lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 share coil current and are not asserted; count 5 = 101: flip-flops A (relays 1, 2) and C (relays 5, 6) at 1, B at 0, so light 5 is off
script.quote: Now push the pushbutton 3 more times and the counter will display the answer—the binary number 5. This is exactly what would have happened had you just pushed the pushbutton 5 times.

script.cite: Book IV printed p.73 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.79, Experiment 2 para 4 (only the low-order three bits are displayed), applied at the eighth push: decimal 8 = 1000 on printed p.68 = PDF p.74 shows as 000; derived from topology: plus reaches the counter only at the relay 1, 3, 5 set-1 N.O. contacts (1G, 3G, 5G) and at the pushbutton 6 arm (6Y); each flip-flop's F node (1F/2F/4A, 3F/4F/5A, 5F/6F/6A) is plus only while its odd relay is latched through its own N.O. (nG-nH), and floats otherwise; a flip-flop at 0 has every node floating, so both its relays rest and its indicator lamps and its output lamp on the E node (outLamp1 on 2E, outLamp2 on 4E, outLamp3 on 6E) carry no current; a flip-flop at 1 has both relays operated (odd relay held through its own indicator lamp, even relay fed from the shared F node) and puts outLamp4, 5 or 6 across the rail; lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 share coil current and are not asserted; the 7-to-8 push carries C to B to A and A has no carry-out wire (relays 1, 2 set 2 unwired), so all three flip-flops return to 0
script.quote: Since we have only three bits in our counter, we would expect to see only the low order three bits of the number displayed.

(nG-nH), and floats otherwise; a flip-flop at 0 has every node floating, so both its relays rest and its indicator lamps and its output lamp on the E node (outLamp1 on 2E, outLamp2 on 4E, outLamp3 on 6E) carry no current; a flip-flop at 1 has both relays operated (odd relay held through its own indicator lamp, even relay fed from the shared F node) and puts outLamp4, 5 or 6 across the rail; lit indicator lamps and lit outLamp1-3 share coil current and are not asserted; count 10 = 1010, low three bits 010: flip-flop B (relays 3, 4) at 1, A and C at 0
script.quote: The bit pattern for the binary equivalent of decimal 10 is 1010. The counter will display 010.
